view.headline: The week the tape sorted itself by hardware, not by risk-on

sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
## The week the tape sorted itself by hardware, not by risk-on

The review window is 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-04 (rotation and sector rows as-of 2026-09-04; the equity, commodity and FX snapshots in the frame carry later as-of stamps and are post-window context, not this week's change). It was a week of within-tech dispersion, not a broad risk rally and not a rates-driven rotation: SPY returned just +0.1% (rotation benchmark, w1), so the semiconductor-hardware surge was relative, not a lifting tide, and with the 10-year (DGS10) at 4.77 down only 2 bp on the week it was not a duration story either.

## Hardware led; software and security lagged, and the spread was wide

The clearest development was intra-semiconductor dispersion. Memory/Storage led the declared sectors at +7.6% (level), +7.5% vs SPY across 4 of 4 priced members, with Computer/GPU at +5.9% (+5.7% vs SPY, 6 of 6 priced) and Foundry at +5.4% (+5.3% vs SPY, 4 of 4 priced). The single-name candidates line up behind that: SNDK led the priced block at +17.2% (window_return, excess_vs_spy +17.1%) and DELL at +14.9% (excess_vs_spy +14.8%), both members of those leading baskets. The mechanism I'd claim is straightforward capacity/AI-hardware demand concentrating in memory and server names; the counterevidence is that relative outperformance alone does not identify a cause, and with SPY flat this is dispersion inside tech rather than a sector the index followed. Against that leadership, Semi-Cap/EDA fell -1.5% (-1.6% vs SPY, 8 of 8 priced) with CDNS -14.0% and SNPS -11.0% (window_return), so the strength did not extend to design tools — a split that argues against a single 'semis are up' narrative. Confirming signal: Memory/Storage holds a positive weekly excess vs SPY next reading. Refuting signal: Semi-Cap/EDA's excess turns positive while Memory/Storage's turns negative, inverting this week's spread.

## Software and cybersecurity were the drag

Cybersecurity was the weakest declared sector at -6.9% (-7.0% vs SPY, 4 of 4 priced), with PANW -10.3% (window_return), and Software/SaaS fell -4.7% (-4.8% vs SPY, 6 of 6 priced), with FIG the second-ranked priced name at -16.3% (excess_vs_spy -16.4%). I will not call the losing sectors a source of funds for the winners — returns do not trace capital transfers — so this is best read as coincident weakness in higher-multiple software while hardware bid. What would change the read: a software/security sector excess that flips positive alongside continued hardware strength would show the two moving together rather than apart. Confirming signal: Cybersecurity weekly excess vs SPY stays negative next reading. Refuting signal: Cybersecurity excess turns positive next reading.

## Ag inputs topped the rotation table

The el-nino-ag-2026 basket (DBA, MOS, NTR, DE equal-weight) posted the largest excess in the rotation table at +6.5% (excess1w) on a +6.6% basket week (w1), extending a +12.9% four-week and +15.7% twelve-week run (rotation w4, w12). DE (excess_vs_spy +9.9%) and MOS (+9.4%) appear directly in the priced candidate block. XLE was the leading GICS sector at +2.2% (w1, +2.1% excess1w), so the strength sits in real-asset and commodity-linked names, consistent with WTI crude at 94.09 (+2.85%) in the frame's commodity snapshot — though that snapshot's as-of is after the review window, so I treat it as context, not the week's driver. The theme's declared kill trigger requires dated NOAA ONI and CBOT inputs I was not handed this run, so I make no claim that any trigger condition is met or unmet. Confirming signal: the ag basket keeps a positive weekly excess vs SPY next reading. Refuting signal: the basket's weekly excess turns negative, ending the four-week lead.

## Backdrop: calm, and I will leave it at that

VIX (VIXCLS) was 14.32, down 0.88 pts, and high-yield spreads (BAMLH0A0HYM2) were 2.65, in 1 bp. I record these as observations only — low vol and tight credit do not by themselves tell me what is priced in or that dips will be bought. The 9/16 hike probability sits at 55.7 (policy.path level) but carries no prior in this frame, so I cannot describe a weekly change in the policy path.

Data limitation: this run's dated-observation reports and the headline feed both returned empty, so the article rests on the frame and rotation payloads alone; I have not reconstructed missing narrative.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
The question next week is whether hardware dispersion persists or mean-reverts. The memory, GPU and foundry leadership rested on demand concentration I can see in the returns but cannot fully attribute; the observable that would confirm persistence is Memory/Storage and Computer/GPU holding positive weekly excess vs SPY into the next reading, while a reversal shows up first in those baskets' excess turning negative even as SPY holds. The reverse risk is that this was a one-week crowding into a few names (SNDK +17.2%, DELL +14.9% window returns) that unwinds; watch whether the design-tool names that lagged this week (Semi-Cap/EDA at -1.5%, CDNS and SNPS both double-digit decliners) catch up, which would argue the whole complex re-rates together rather than the narrow hardware slice leading alone.

Software and cybersecurity enter next week as the laggards (Software/SaaS -4.7%, Cybersecurity -6.9% weekly). The near-term tell here is Adobe: the frame admits ADBE earnings post-close on 2026-09-10, inside the coming seven days, with an implied move of 6.9333% and an ivRank of 68.84 — the market is pricing a real event, and Adobe's recent completed prints (actual eps 4.58 on 2026-06-11, 4.83 on 2026-03-12, both postmarket, company-sourced) are the historical backdrop rather than a guide to direction. A soft software print could deepen the sector's relative weakness; a strong one could be the first sign the group's lag is idiosyncratic, not structural.

The ag/commodity leadership is the most durable-looking move on the multi-week rotation numbers (ag basket +12.9% four-week, +15.7% twelve-week; XLE +11.4% four-week). What would keep it going is continued positive weekly excess; what would break it is the basket's weekly excess turning negative. I cannot assess the theme's NOAA/CBOT kill inputs this run because they were not supplied, so I hold the view as trend-following, not fundamentally confirmed.

On the macro backdrop, the 9/16 policy decision is later context, not a coming-seven-days event, and I have no dated prior to characterise how the hike probability moved this week. Rates were nearly unchanged (10-year 4.77, -2 bp) and vol and credit were calm; I would watch whether that calm coexists with the next equity reading or whether a single catalyst widens spreads or lifts VIX, which is the condition that would turn this from a dispersion week into a directional one.
